correctness.rationale: The two schedules have the same duration 2m per two pulses, so their comparison is the centered second difference of F(t)=e^(−bt)[1−(1+at)e^(−at)]. Writing c=a+b and J=cosh(cd)−1, the normalized difference is B−H with B=cosh(bd)−1 and H=e^(−am)[(1+am)J−ad sinh(cd)]. The derivative has the sign of d sinh(cd)−mJ, giving the interior peak m*=d coth(cd/2). For z=cd/2, log(sinh(z)/sinh(bz/c))=∫ from bz/c to z of coth(v) dv, strictly greater than a m*/2 by strict decrease of coth. This proves H(m*)>B, while H tends to zero at infinity. Hence one upper root always exists, and the lower one is admissible exactly when F(2d)>2F(d). For G(x)=1−(1+x)e^(−x), its elasticity xG′/G is x²/(e^x−1−x), strictly decreasing because its reciprocal has a positive-coefficient power series with positive linear term. Therefore e^(−bd)G(2ad)/G(ad) strictly decreases from 4 to 0, giving the unique threshold. At equality m=d itself is excluded and there is only the upper admissible root. With a single stage the normalized gap is strictly increasing from a negative value to B>0. Independent decimal bisection of the original differences reproduced d_c=0.425304912003236…, the roots 0.372551797020654… and 2.16039402036334… for a=b=1,d=0.2 and all three illustrated percentages. Finite diagnostics are supplementary; uploaded code was not run.
residual_risks: The conclusion is exact for positive a,b,C,d and m>d, under a fresh independently initialized cohort and an instantaneous reward at rewetting. It does not extend to arbitrary maturation, survival or cycle-memory laws.

evidence: Manzoni et al. use a stochastic rainfall/soil-moisture state and a pulse determined by antecedent moisture and moisture change. Fierer–Schimel compare experimentally controlled frequencies using evenly spaced cycles.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Empirical frequency effects and state-dependent pulses do not give the stated fresh-cohort reward. The exponential-polynomial shape or a zero-count bound explains why two crossings are possible but does not establish the strict peak comparison or the admission threshold at m=d.

evidence: The fish-passage result integrates passage-time densities weighted by survival only up to completion, and compares one- and two-stage designs at a single deadline. Here survival must continue through rewetting and the one- and two-stage models are each compared at three lags m−d,m,m+d.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The survival-weighted integral cannot be substituted for a survival-at-deadline product; it can converge to a positive probability, while the stated pulse tends to zero. Its mortality threshold and root disappearance do not imply the dry-spell half-gap threshold or signs. The inspected soil models likewise do not specify that comparison.

evidence: Equal average duration means comparing the two-point symmetric average to the value at its midpoint; its sign is exactly the sign of D_d F(m), where F=e^(−bt)−(1+at)e^(−(a+b)t). The direct indexed match is the assigned record.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The algebraic centered-difference formulation removes the ecological terminology without changing the claim. Exact equivalence was not established with a distinct indexed entry; the search miss alone does not justify novelty.

value.rationale: Under a natural equal-mean, equal-event-count control, a response requiring maturation and survival creates two finite sign reversals, which a one-stage model does not allow. The all-parameter diagram shows exactly when that second reversal is lost and whether it is lost through the schedule boundary; neither a local curvature heuristic nor a numerical plot settles those questions. This is useful as a diagnostic benchmark for idealized cycle-pulse modeling, not as a quantitative field prediction.
residual_risks: The simple kernel may not be field calibrated; total soil respiration, substrate carryover and variable precipitation intensity are outside the claim.
